counterfactual_missing_items: No clear evidence of tau protein pathology
No mention of typical progressive supranuclear palsy symptoms such as postural instability
decisive_items: Heterozygous pathogenic variant of TBK1 gene (p.E643del) identified by whole-exon sequencing
response.rationale: The presence of a heterozygous pathogenic variant of the TBK1 gene, along with symptoms such as tongue atrophy and vertical gaze palsy, strongly supports the diagnosis of frontotemporal dementia and parkinsonism-17 due to TBK1 gene variant

rejected.why: Lack of clear evidence for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis as the primary diagnosis, despite some consistent symptoms
Insufficient evidence to support progressive supranuclear palsy as the primary diagnosis, given the presence of a TBK1 gene variant and other inconsistent symptoms
